transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~37 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hall (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NovaHealth - Lead ML Engineer), Tom Reynolds (NovaHealth - Infra Engineer), Grace Park (NovaHealth - PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding progress, confirming staging access, KMS/SSO handoff, and a small latency bench plan. SE will run targeted micro-benchmarks; customer will provision KMS and share prompt set. Agreed to security deep-dive next week.

Topics:
- Access status (SSO, KMS, VPC peering)
- Bench plan (latency, 95/99, throughput headroom)
- KV cache / prefix caching expectations
- Rollback/fallback for model variants
- Next steps and ownership

Action items recap (read out): Lena to send runbook; Marcus to run bench; Tom to provision KMS; Aisha to send prompts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we did a short agenda, want to keep this to 30-ish minutes, but we have 37 so, uh, that's fine.
[00:18] Aisha (NovaHealth): Yep, good here. Sorry, running a little late, pulled in Grace and Tom.
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): Morning! I'll jump to the bench details after we confirm access.
[00:28] Grace (NovaHealth): Morning — real quick: timeline — we want a staging greenlight by next Friday, is that still realistic?
[00:35] Lena: That's the goal. If we get KMS and SSO in place this week and Marcus pushes the micro-bench, we can validate SLA targets and be comfortable with a greenlight.
[00:45] Tom: On KMS — I started provisioning, but wanted to confirm Redwood's expected key policies. Do you need symmetric keys or an envelope setup?
[00:53] Marcus: We support both; envelope is preferred. We'll provide the policy template. Also we'll need an IAM principal for service-to-service access — we'll send the ARN pattern.
[01:05] Aisha: Ok, noted. Also curious: how does prefix caching behave if we have high variation in prompt prefixes across patients? Will it still help?
[01:12] Marcus: Good question. Prefix/KV cache helps when you have repeated session context or templates. If your prefixes are high-cardinality, hit-rate drops. We can tune TTLs and eviction and use partial caching for embeddings reranking to get win. But yeah, if it's entirely unique every time, cache hit is low.
[01:28] Grace: Is there a way to simulate real traffic during bench? We have different prompt lengths and some stop sequences.
[01:33] Marcus: Absolutely — please send the prompt set. We'll run a mixed-profile bench: short, medium, long; measure p50/p95/p99 and token-level cost. We'll also run a KV-cold vs KV-warm test to quantify cache benefits.
[01:45] Tom: On network — we planned VPC peering. Any specifics on egress IPs to allow for the staging gateway?
[01:52] Lena: We'll share the ephemeral egress list for the region, but for the private deploys you'll be peering directly. For hosted staging we'll provide a static NAT IP range for allowlisting.
[02:05] Aisha: Security question: audit logs and data residency. We need to make sure we capture request/response provenance without storing PHI in Redwood logs.
[02:12] Lena: Understood. Redwood can redact payloads at ingest and provide metadata-level audit logs. For PHI use we recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity with configurable retention. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and the data retention matrix.
[02:25] Tom: Are there encryption-in-transit cert expectations? Our infra team is strict about mutual TLS.
[02:30] Marcus: Mutual TLS is supported for private deployments. For hosted, we use mTLS for customer gateways; we can also support client certs — we'll outline options in the runbook.
[02:40] Grace: Great. Back to the bench: what's a realistic throughput to try? We were thinking 50 QPS burst up to 200 for peak.
[02:48] Marcus: Start with 50 steady QPS, then step to 100, 150, 200 — measure p95/p99, and observe KV cache hit-rate and GPU queue times. We'll also capture memory/KV-residency metrics.
[03:05] Aisha: Any guidance on quantization profiles? We're worried about quality drop with aggressive quant.
[03:12] Marcus: We'll recommend two quant profiles: conservative (8-bit) and aggressive (4-bit) for cost testing. We'll run the same prompt set and report delta in top-1 logits and hallucination regressions. You can pick the tradeoff.
[03:25] Lena: For the staging handoff, we need Tom to confirm KMS, and Aisha to provide prompts. Marcus will run the bench. I will send the staging access runbook with the checklist for SSO, egress, and KMS binding.
[03:39] Tom: Quick note — our infra team needs a runbook link, otherwise they'll block.
[03:42] Lena: I'll put the runbook in the shared drive and drop link in the slack thread after the call.
[03:50] Grace: On success criteria: we care about <120ms median token latency and p99 under 700ms for our interactive flows; offline tasks can be slower. Also budget target per 1k tokens.
[04:05] Marcus: We'll aim to show whether the hosted config meets that. If not, we can propose dedicated or model-variant fallback to meet latency SLOs.
[04:15] Aisha: If we hit a p99 of 900ms on hosted, is dedicated an immediate red flag?
[04:20] Marcus: Not immediate; dedicated can bring down variance and give more predictable p99s. Also quant and batching config can significantly change p99. We'll explore knobs first.
[04:34] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — sorry, crossed audio there.
[04:37] Lena: No worries. Ok, schedule: security deep-dive next Monday, bench results by Wednesday, runbook by tomorrow. Everyone good with that?
[04:45] Grace: Yes.
[04:46] Tom: Yes.
[04:47] Aisha: Yep.
[04:48] Marcus: One more thing — fallback policy. If a model variant is unavailable, Redwood can route to a smaller model automatically; do you want us to enable auto-fallback for the pilot?
[04:55] Grace: We'd prefer explicit control for now — manual fallback during the POC.
[04:59] Marcus: Understood. We'll set the policy to manual.
[05:02] Lena: Great, I'll capture that. Any other risks?
[05:06] Aisha: None from me. We'll get prompts over.
[05:10] Tom: I'll confirm KMS and VPC peering details tonight.
[05:14] Grace: I'll finalize the success criteria doc and share it.
[05:18] Lena: Thanks everyone. I'll put notes and runbook link in slack and email. We'll reconvene next week for the security deep-dive.
[05:27] Marcus: Bye all.
[05:28] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlap and background noise; some product names may be transcribed slightly off (K V cache vs KV cache).
